are simulated; these exercises cannot establish a finding about a real disease.
See the [glossary](../docs/glossary.md) for the course vocabulary. Each module
loads its inputs from disk; a saved R workspace is not required.

```{r module7_setup, include=FALSE}
if (requireNamespace("knitr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(if (file.exists("config.R")) "." else ".."))
}
source("R/guided.R")
cfg <- guided_init()
```

## 7.1 QQ plot {#step-7-1}

### What we do

Compare the distribution of observed autosomal association p-values with a uniform-null reference.

### Why

A quantile?quantile (QQ) plot pairs ordered observed values with the values expected under a reference distribution. Under calibrated null tests, p-values are approximately uniform; ?log10 transforms small values into large positive values. A few strong associations lift the extreme tail. Broad deviation can reflect confounding, technical problems, model misspecification or many true small effects. A visual deviation alone cannot distinguish them. Correlated variants also mean the points are not independent observations.

### You need

The adjusted association scan from 6.4.

### Command

```{r s7-1}
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
autosomal <- results$CHROM %in% as.character(1:22)
save_plot(guided_path(cfg, "7.1", "qq.png"), function() plot_qq(results$P[autosomal], "Adjusted simulated GWAS: autosomal QQ plot"))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
No PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.
```

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

Most points are close to the null diagonal, with a strong upper-tail departure. Missing, zero or invalid p-values are not plotted as arbitrary significant values.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks, instructor comparisons and final plot checks passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Does a strong departure affecting only the extreme tail necessarily imply genome-wide confounding?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. A few true signals can lift the tail while most null tests remain calibrated.

</details>

### Files created

`s7-1_qq.png`.

Figure placeholder. Gemini prompt: Draw a teaching QQ schematic showing a diagonal null distribution, a tail-only departure and broad inflation in separate labelled panels. Explain possible causes without labelling every departure confounding; use line styles and text as well as colour.

## 7.2 Genomic inflation factor {#step-7-2}

### What we do

Calculate autosomal lambda and interpret it alongside the QQ plot.

### Why

Genomic inflation factor lambda is the median one-degree-of-freedom chi-square statistic divided by its null median, approximately 0.4549. We convert each valid p-value using the chi-square upper-tail quantile. A value near one is consistent with median calibration, not proof of no confounding. Lambda depends on sample size, polygenicity, phenotype model and tested variant set. Do not automatically divide every test by lambda or treat one threshold as a pass/fail diagnosis.

### You need

The same autosomal p-values used at 7.1.

### Command

```{r s7-2}
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
p <- results$P[results$CHROM %in% as.character(1:22)]
lambda <- lambda_gc(p)
print(lambda)
stopifnot(abs(lambda - 1.016) < 0.001)
guided_write(data.frame(model = "QC plus ten PCs", lambda = lambda), guided_path(cfg, "7.2", "lambda.tsv"))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
No PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.
```

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

Lambda approximately 1.016, computed from valid autosomal tests. The test uses the same definition as the reference run.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks, instructor comparisons and final plot checks passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Can lambda near one prove that a particular lead is causal?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. Lambda summarises the median test distribution, not the validity or causal interpretation of an individual association.

</details>

### Files created

`s7-2_lambda.tsv`.

## 7.3 Manhattan plot {#step-7-3}

### What we do

Plot association evidence along the autosomal genome.

### Why

A Manhattan plot places chromosome and position on the horizontal axis and ?log10(p) vertically. Nearby high points can be correlated through LD and may represent one region. Position identifies where evidence is observed, not which gene causes an effect. The axis uses GRCh38 throughout. Alternating colours separate chromosomes; chromosome labels and position order also carry that information.

### You need

The full adjusted results from 6.4.

### Command

```{r s7-3}
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
plot_data <- results
plot_data$CHROM <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(plot_data$CHROM))
save_plot(guided_path(cfg, "7.3", "manhattan.png"), function() plot_manhattan(plot_data, "Simulated GWAS: age, sex and ten PCs"))
stopifnot(sum(results$P[valid_p(results$P)] < 5e-8) == 8L)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
No PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.
```

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

Three strong regions on chromosomes 3, 9 and 12, comprising eight variants below 5?10??. The moderate planted region does not reach that conventional threshold. Non-autosomal tests remain in the result table but are not placed on this autosomal figure.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks, instructor comparisons and final plot checks passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Do four nearby significant variants necessarily imply four independent causal effects?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. LD can make several tested variants tag the same underlying signal.

</details>

`s7-3_manhattan.png`.

## 7.4 Multiple-testing thresholds {#step-7-4}

### What we do

Compare the conventional GWAS threshold, scan-specific Bonferroni and false-discovery-rate adjustment.

### Why

Testing many null hypotheses creates many opportunities for false positives. Bonferroni divides a chosen family-wise error rate alpha by the number of tests; it controls the probability of at least one false rejection under its assumptions even when tests are dependent. The conventional 5?10?? threshold approximates 0.05 divided by one million common-variant tests; it is a convention, not a guarantee for every ancestry, sequencing design or analysis family. Benjamini?Hochberg (BH) targets a different quantity: the expected fraction of false discoveries among rejected tests under its conditions. Define the test family before inspecting results.

### You need

Valid additive results from 6.4; no replacement of failed p-values.

### Command

```{r s7-4}
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
p <- results$P[valid_p(results$P)]
threshold <- data.frame(rule = c("Conventional GWAS", "Bonferroni for this scan", "BH adjusted p at 0.05"),
  threshold = c(5e-8, 0.05 / length(p), 0.05),
  discoveries = c(sum(p < 5e-8), sum(p < 0.05 / length(p)), sum(p.adjust(p, method = "BH") < 0.05)))
print(threshold)
guided_write(threshold, guided_path(cfg, "7.4", "thresholds.tsv"))
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
No PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.
```

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

236,815 finite tests imply a scan-specific Bonferroni threshold of approximately 2.11?10??. The conventional threshold gives eight discoveries. BH answers a different error-control question and may return more.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks, instructor comparisons and final plot checks passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Does FDR 5% mean each reported variant has a 5% probability of being false?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. FDR is an expectation about the discovery set, not a posterior probability assigned to each variant.

</details>

### Files created

`s7-4_thresholds.tsv`.

## 7.5 Clump correlated results {#step-7-5}

### What we do

Group correlated significant variants around index variants using study-cohort LD.

### Why

Clumping starts with the smallest p-value, assigns nearby correlated variants, and continues greedily. It describes approximately independent regions under chosen radius and LD settings. It is not fine-mapping, causal inference or proof of one causal effect per clump. Use LD from the analysed cohort rather than an unmatched external population.

### You need

The full 5.7 genotype set and unaltered PLINK association report from 6.4.

### Command

```{r s7-5}
report <- guided_path(cfg, "7.5", "clump")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "5.7"), "--clump", paste0(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"), ".Disease.glm.logistic.hybrid"),
  "--clump-id-field", "ID", "--clump-p-field", "P", "--clump-p1", "5e-8", "--clump-p2", "1e-5",
  "--clump-r2", "0.1", "--clump-kb", "250", "--clump-unphased", "--out", report))
clumps <- guided_table(paste0(report, ".clumps"))
print(clumps)
stopifnot(nrow(clumps) == 3L)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s5-7_state --clump results/guided/s6-4_association.Disease.glm.logistic.hybrid --clump-id-field ID --clump-p-field P --clump-p1 5e-8 --clump-p2 1e-5 --clump-r2 0.1 --clump-kb 250 --clump-unphased --out results/guided/s7-5_clump --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--clump` reads the association report. `--clump-id-field ID` and `--clump-p-field P` name its columns. `--clump-p1 5e-8` sets index eligibility and `--clump-p2 1e-5` the secondary-report threshold. `--clump-r2 0.1` uses this correlation threshold within `--clump-kb 250` kilobases. `--clump-unphased` uses squared dosage correlation, making its LD definition explicit. `--out` names the report; threads and memory are set by the helper.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

Three clumps describing the strong chromosome 3, 9 and 12 regions. Their index IDs and p-values are reported; this does not establish three causal variants.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks, instructor comparisons and final plot checks passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

If the LD threshold or radius changes, can the clump membership change even though the association scan is identical?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

Yes. Clump membership is conditional on those settings and the LD sample.

</details>

### Files created

`s7-5_clump.clumps` and logs.

## 7.6 Regional plot {#step-7-6}

### What we do

Examine the L2 region with LD relative to its lead variant.

### Why

A regional plot separates position, association evidence and LD. L2 on chromosome 9 is used because L1 has only one genome-wide significant variant in this array subset. Nearby points with high r? to the lead can share association evidence. Low LD or several local peaks do not on their own establish multiple causal effects. No gene assignment or post-GWAS annotation is attempted here.

### You need

Main results, final cohort and the lead 9:96426973:A:G from the chromosome 9 clump.

### Command

```{r s7-6}
lead <- "9:96426973:A:G"
report <- guided_path(cfg, "7.6", "ld")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "5.7"), "--chr", "9", "--from-bp", "95926973", "--to-bp", "96926973",
  "--r2-unphased", "--ld-snp", lead, "--ld-window-kb", "500", "--ld-window-r2", "0", "--out", report))
ld <- guided_table(paste0(report, ".vcor"))
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
region <- results[results$CHROM == "9" & abs(results$POS - 96426973) <= 500000 & valid_p(results$P), ]
r2_column <- grep("R2$", names(ld), value = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(r2_column) == 1L)
r2 <- as.numeric(ld[[r2_column]][match(region$ID, ld$ID_B)])
r2[region$ID == lead] <- 1
bin <- cut(r2, breaks = c(-0.01, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1.01), include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE)
colours <- c("#0072B2", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#E69F00", "#D55E00")
shapes <- c(1, 2, 3, 4, 16)
png(guided_path(cfg, "7.6", "regional.png"), width = 1400, height = 900, res = 150)
plot(region$POS / 1e6, -log10(region$P), col = ifelse(is.na(bin), "#666666", colours[bin]),
  pch = ifelse(is.na(bin), 8, shapes[bin]), xlab = "GRCh38 chromosome 9 position (Mb)", ylab = "-log10(p)", main = "L2: association and LD to the lead")
abline(h = -log10(5e-8), lty = 2)
legend("topright", legend = c("r2: 0 to 0.2", "0.2 to 0.4", "0.4 to 0.6", "0.6 to 0.8", "0.8 to 1", "LD unavailable"),
  pch = c(shapes, 8), col = c(colours, "#666666"), cex = 0.8)
dev.off()
stopifnot(sum(region$P < 5e-8) == 4L)
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "7.6", c(paste0(report, ".vcor"), guided_path(cfg, "7.6", "regional.png")), parent = "6.7")
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s5-7_state --chr 9 --from-bp 95926973 --to-bp 96926973 --r2-unphased --ld-snp 9:96426973:A:G --ld-window-kb 500 --ld-window-r2 0 --out results/guided/s7-6_ld --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--chr 9`, `--from-bp` and `--to-bp` define a one-megabase GRCh38 interval. `--r2-unphased` reports squared dosage correlation. `--ld-snp` restricts the first member of pairs to the lead. `--ld-window-kb 500` limits distance from it and `--ld-window-r2 0` retains low as well as high correlations; otherwise low-LD points could disappear from the report. `--out`, threads and memory have the meanings given earlier.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

Four genome-wide significant variants in L2. The plot encodes LD by symbol and colour; a missing LD value is labelled unavailable rather than silently set to zero.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks, instructor comparisons and final plot checks passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Does the highest point necessarily identify the causal variant?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. The lead is the strongest observed association among tested sites and may tag an unmeasured cause.

</details>

### Files created

`s7-6_ld.vcor`, `s7-6_regional.png` and the regional analysis checkpoint.

## 7.7 Compare without PCs and without QC {#step-7-7}

### What we do

Contrast the prespecified main analysis with two deliberately less-adjusted analyses.

### Why

First omit PCs while keeping the same cleaned cohort and covariates age/sex. That isolates the PC adjustment contrast. Then analyse the phenotype-labelled, strand-harmonised module 2 state without sample or variant QC and without PCs. This second contrast changes cohort and site composition as well as QC, so its differences cannot be attributed to one cause alone. The no-QC label does not mean strand harmonisation or phenotype matching was undone. Compare shared variants and per-variant sample counts when interpreting differences.

### You need

State 5.7, boundary 2.8, main association report, covariates and original metadata.

### Command

```{r s7-7}
no_pc <- guided_path(cfg, "7.7", "no_pcs")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "5.7"), "--maf", "0.01", "--covar", guided_path(cfg, "6.3", "covariates.tsv"),
  "--covar-name", "Age", "--covar-variance-standardize", "--glm", "sex", "hide-covar", "firth-fallback", "--out", no_pc))
metadata <- guided_metadata(cfg)
all_covar <- metadata[c("FID", "IID", "Age")]; names(all_covar)[1] <- "#FID"
all_file <- guided_path(cfg, "7.7", "all_ages.tsv"); guided_write(all_covar, all_file)
no_qc <- guided_path(cfg, "7.7", "no_qc_no_pcs")
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "2.8"), "--maf", "0.01", "--covar", all_file,
  "--covar-name", "Age", "--covar-variance-standardize", "--glm", "sex", "hide-covar", "firth-fallback", "--out", no_qc))
main <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
a <- guided_association(no_pc); b <- guided_association(no_qc)
k <- match(main$ID, a$ID)
stopifnot(!anyNA(k), all(main$OBS_CT == a$OBS_CT[k]))
summarise <- function(x) c(finite_tests = sum(valid_p(x$P)), hits = sum(x$P[valid_p(x$P)] < 5e-8),
  lambda = lambda_gc(x$P[x$CHROM %in% as.character(1:22)]))
comparison <- rbind(main = summarise(main), no_PCs = summarise(a), no_sample_or_variant_QC_no_PCs = summarise(b))
print(comparison)
stopifnot(comparison[2, "hits"] == 15L, comparison[3, "hits"] == 19L)
guided_write(data.frame(model = rownames(comparison), comparison, row.names = NULL), guided_path(cfg, "7.7", "comparison.tsv"))
save_plot(guided_path(cfg, "7.7", "qq_comparison.png"), function() {
  par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
  plotted <- list(main$P[main$CHROM %in% as.character(1:22)], a$P[a$CHROM %in% as.character(1:22)], b$P[b$CHROM %in% as.character(1:22)])
  limits <- c(0, max(-log10(unlist(plotted))))
  plot_qq(main$P[main$CHROM %in% as.character(1:22)], "QC + ten PCs", ylim = limits)
  plot_qq(a$P[a$CHROM %in% as.character(1:22)], "QC, no PCs", ylim = limits)
  plot_qq(b$P[b$CHROM %in% as.character(1:22)], "No sample/variant QC, no PCs", ylim = limits)
}, width = 2100, height = 750)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s5-7_state --maf 0.01 --covar results/guided/s6-3_covariates.tsv --covar-name Age --covar-variance-standardize --glm sex hide-covar firth-fallback --out results/guided/s7-7_no_pcs --threads 2 --memory 2048
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s2-8_state --maf 0.01 --covar results/guided/s7-7_all_ages.tsv --covar-name Age --covar-variance-standardize --glm sex hide-covar firth-fallback --out results/guided/s7-7_no_qc_no_pcs --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

The same `--glm sex hide-covar firth-fallback` settings are used throughout. `--covar-name Age` omits PCs explicitly. The first call retains the cleaned cohort; the second changes `--pfile` to the pre-QC boundary and uses ages for all wells. `--maf 0.01` remains an association eligibility rule even in the no-QC contrast. `--out` separates outputs; threads and memory are unchanged.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>

Main: 236,815 tests, eight hits, lambda about 1.016. Without PCs after QC: 236,815 tests, 15 hits, lambda about 1.546. Without sample/variant QC or PCs: 239,647 tests, 19 hits, lambda about 1.655. The extra peaks are not evidence that worse QC finds more true causes.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks, instructor comparisons and final plot checks passed on Windows.

</details>

<details><summary>If something goes wrong</summary>

Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).

</details>

### Quick check

Can the main versus no-PC comparison be interpreted more narrowly than the main versus no-QC comparison?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

Yes. The first keeps the same analysed genotype cohort and per-variant counts, while the second also changes samples and tested sites.

</details>

### Files created

Two comparison association outputs, age table, `s7-7_comparison.tsv` and `s7-7_qq_comparison.png`.

## 7.8 Final summary and reporting {#step-7-8}

### What we do

Write an auditable summary of the complete simulated main path and save its final analysis artifacts.

### Why

A report must connect the study design, QC decisions, model, effect estimates, uncertainty and figures. Include assembly, software versions, sample counts, exclusions, PCs, tested allele and threshold. Distinguish observed associations from causal claims and simulated teaching signals from biological discoveries. A null or subthreshold result can reflect limited statistical power, meaning the chance to detect an effect of a given size under the study design. Retain a reproducible record without publishing person-level data.

### You need

Verified modules 0?6, figures and comparisons from 7.1?7.7.

### Command

```{r s7-8}
psam <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "5.7"), ".psam"))
comparison <- read.delim(guided_path(cfg, "7.7", "comparison.tsv"))
clumps <- guided_table(paste0(guided_path(cfg, "7.5", "clump"), ".clumps"))
results <- guided_association(guided_path(cfg, "6.4", "association"))
lead <- results[match(clumps$ID, results$ID), c("CHROM", "POS", "ID", "A1", "OR", "LOG(OR)_SE", "P", "OBS_CT")]
lead$CI_LOW <- exp(log(lead$OR) - 1.96 * lead[["LOG(OR)_SE"]])
lead$CI_HIGH <- exp(log(lead$OR) + 1.96 * lead[["LOG(OR)_SE"]])
guided_write(lead, guided_path(cfg, "7.8", "leads.tsv"))
summary <- c("# Simulated GWAS: main-path summary", "", "Genome assembly: GRCh38. Simulated data, seed 20261111.",
  paste("Software:", paste(cfg$version, collapse = "; ")),
  "Initial: 2,016 measured wells, 2,000 people, 299,523 variant entries.",
  paste("Final cohort:", nrow(psam), "samples; cases:", sum(psam$Disease == "2"), "; controls:", sum(psam$Disease == "1")),
  "After QC: 238,513 variants; 236,815 finite additive association tests.",
  "Model: additive logistic regression, adjusted for age, recorded sex and ten within-cohort PCs; Firth fallback enabled.",
  "Eight variants pass p < 5e-8 in three LD clumps. Autosomal lambda is approximately 1.016.",
  "Report A1, OR, 95% interval, p-value and per-variant OBS_CT from s7-8_leads.tsv.",
  "Interpretation: the three strong simulated regions are recovered; the moderate region is subthreshold. No causal gene is established.",
  "Sensitivity: omitting PCs increases lambda to approximately 1.546; omitting sample/variant QC as well gives approximately 1.655.",
  "Limitations: simulated design, selected array sites, finite power, provisional imported REF labels, study-specific QC and ancestry rules.",
  "Three named ancestry markers left at HWE step 4.4; comparisons must not pretend they survived to module 5.",
  "Figures: s7-1_qq.png, s7-3_manhattan.png, s7-6_regional.png and s7-7_qq_comparison.png.",
  "No biological discovery or clinical recommendation follows from this simulation.")
writeLines(summary, guided_path(cfg, "7.8", "summary.md"), useBytes = TRUE)
files <- c(guided_path(cfg, "7.8", "summary.md"), guided_path(cfg, "7.8", "leads.tsv"),
  guided_path(cfg, "7.1", "qq.png"), guided_path(cfg, "7.3", "manhattan.png"),
  guided_path(cfg, "7.6", "regional.png"), guided_path(cfg, "7.7", "qq_comparison.png"),
  guided_path(cfg, "7.7", "comparison.tsv"), paste0(guided_path(cfg, "7.5", "clump"), ".clumps"),
  file.path(cfg$out, "step_counts.tsv"), file.path(cfg$out, "software_versions.txt"))
guided_artifact_checkpoint(cfg, "7.8", files, parent = "6.7")
check_step("7.8", data_dir = cfg$out, work_dir = cfg$out)
cat(paste(summary, collapse = "\n"), "\n")
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
No PLINK operation is needed for this R-only or laboratory step. The R chunk is the complete command; PLINK cannot perform a laboratory measurement.
```

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.

<details><summary>Show the expected result</summary>
